accepted.name: differential_expression_by_gene_disease
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  gene_symbol,
  doid,
  log2fc,
  pvalue,
  adjpvalue,
  statistical_significance,
  expression_change_direction,
  subjects_up,
  subjects_down,
  subjects_nochange,
  subjects_nocoverage,
  subjects_total
FROM differential_expression
accepted.description: Normalized/deduplicated differential expression measurements at the gene_symbol + doid grain with preserved statistical and subject-count fields. Useful as a cleaned projection for downstream joins, filtering by significance, or aggregations by gene or disease. | Use for: Which genes are differentially expressed for a disease (by doid)?; Filter differential expression results by significance or fold-change and join to gene/biomarker tables; Aggregate number of significant genes per disease or compare subject counts across diseases

accepted.name: healthy_expression_by_gene_anatomy
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ensembl_gene_id,
  uberon_anatomical_id,
  uberon_developmental_id,
  expression_level_gene_relative,
  expression_level_anatomical_relative,
  call_quality,
  expression_rank_score,
  expression_score
FROM healthy_expression
accepted.description: Projection of healthy tissue expression calls at the ensembl_gene_id + uberon_anatomical_id + uberon_developmental_id grain including expression scores and ranks. Useful for tissue-specific expression lookups and joins to anatomical entities or gene mappings. | Use for: What tissues show high expression for a given gene (by ensembl_gene_id)?; Compare expression ranks/scores across anatomical terms or developmental stages; Join to anatomical_entity to show tissue names for expression records

accepted.name: biomarker_with_aliases_and_articles
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description,
  b.biomarker_id,
  b.test_is_a_panel,
  ba.alias,
  ba.biomarker_internal_id AS biomarker_internal_id,
  ba.alias AS alias_from_ba,
  ba.alias AS alias_duplicate_holder,
  bm.pmid
FROM biomarker b
LEFT JOIN biomarker_alias ba
  ON ba.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_article bm
  ON bm.biomarker_internal_id = b.id
accepted.description: Denormalized biomarker-level relation joining biomarker core attributes with all aliases and linked article PMIDs. One row per biomarker alias + article combination (multiplicative). Useful for text/display, filtering by alias or PMID, or aggregating counts of aliases/articles per biomarker. | Use for: List biomarkers with their aliases and supporting literature; Count number of aliases or articles per biomarker; Filter biomarkers by alias text or PMID and join back to biomarker attributes

accepted.name: biomarker_fda_tests_w_drugs_ncit
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  bf.id,
  bf.test_trade_name,
  bf.test_submission,
  bft.test_manufacturer,
  bft.biomarker_origin,
  bft.doid,
  bft.histological_type,
  bft.specimen_type,
  bft.platform_method,
  bft.test_number_genes,
  bft.test_adoption_evidence,
  bft.test_approval_status,
  bft.test_study_design,
  bft.clinical_significance,
  bfdd.biomarker_drug,
  bfn.ncit_biomarker
FROM biomarker_fda bf
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test bft
  ON bft.test_trade_name = bf.test_trade_name
  AND bft.test_submission = bf.test_submission
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_drug bfdd
  ON bfdd.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_ncit_term bfn
  ON bfn.biomarker_fda_id = bf.id
accepted.description: Denormalized view of FDA biomarker/test metadata joining biomarker_fda, biomarker_fda_test, related drugs, and NCIt terms. One row per test_trade_name + test_submission + drug + ncit term combination (multiplicative). Useful for exploring test attributes alongside drugs and ontology terms or aggregating drug lists per test. | Use for: Which FDA tests target a given disease (doid) or histological type?; List drugs associated with an FDA biomarker/test and related ontology terms; Aggregate tests by approval status or manufacturer

accepted.name: disease_mutation_with_annotations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.id,
  dm.chromosome_id,
  dm.chromosome_pos,
  dm.ref_nt,
  dm.alt_nt,
  dm.ensembl_transcript_id,
  dm.cds_pos,
  dm.peptide_pos,
  dm.aa_pos_uniprotkb,
  dm.ref_aa,
  dm.alt_aa,
  dm.mutation_freq,
  dm.data_source,
  dm.doid,
  dma.pmid,
  dmip.site_prediction,
  dmip.probability,
  dmip.tool,
  dmsa.description AS site_description,
  dmsa.feature_key,
  dmt.uberon_anatomical_id
FROM disease_mutation dm
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_article dma
  ON dma.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_impact_prediction dmip
  ON dmip.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_site_annotation dmsa
  ON dmsa.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
LEFT JOIN disease_mutation_tissue dmt
  ON dmt.disease_mutation_id = dm.id
accepted.description: Mutation-centric view joining disease_mutation with related articles, impact predictions, site annotations, and tissue mappings. One row per disease_mutation plus any related annotation/prediction/article/tissue (multiplicative). Useful for surfacing mutation context, evidence pmids, predicted impacts, and tissue associations. | Use for: What annotations and evidence exist for a given mutation id?; Find mutations occurring in a given tissue (uberon id) or associated with high-impact predictions; Aggregate number of articles or predictions per mutation

accepted.name: gene_ensembl_to_uniprot_map
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  x.gene_symbol,
  x.ensembl_gene_id,
  x.speciesid,
  mpd.uniprotkb_ac,
  muc.uniprotkb_canonical_ac
FROM xref_gene_ensembl x
LEFT JOIN map_protein_disease_mutation mpd
  ON mpd.ensembl_transcript_id = x.ensembl_gene_id
LEFT JOIN map_uniprot_canonical_id muc
  ON muc.uniprotkb_ac = mpd.uniprotkb_ac
accepted.description: Mapping from gene_symbol/ensembl_gene_id to UniProt canonical accession where available by chaining xref_gene_ensembl -> map_protein_disease_mutation -> map_uniprot_canonical_id. One row per ensembl_gene_id + uniprotkb_ac mapping. Useful when linking gene-centric results to protein identifiers. | Use for: Map gene symbols/ensembl ids to UniProt accessions; Join proteomic data (Uniprot) back to gene- or transcript-level observations; Resolve canonical UniProt accession for downstream aggregation by protein

accepted.name: anatomical_entity_lookup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  description
FROM anatomical_entity
accepted.description: Simple projection of anatomical entities (ontology id and descriptive fields). Useful as a stable dimension to join to expression, EDRN or mutation tissue mappings. | Use for: Show human-readable tissue names for uberon ids; Filter anatomical entities by name and join to expression or mutation tissue tables

accepted.name: disease_summary
accepted.description: Projection of disease table useful as a stable dimension for joins to mutation or FDA test disease identifiers (doid). | Use for: Lookup disease names for doid values; Join disease names to mutation or test records

accepted.name: biomarker_edrn_with_anatomy
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  be.id,
  be.qa_state,
  be.biomarker_title,
  be.biomarker_type,
  be.uberon_anatomical_id,
  ae.name AS anatomical_name,
  be.phase
FROM biomarker_edrn be
LEFT JOIN anatomical_entity ae
  ON ae.id = be.uberon_anatomical_id
accepted.description: EDRN biomarker records joined to anatomical entity names where uberon_anatomical_id matches anatomical_entity.id. One row per biomarker_edrn record; anatomy may be NULL if no match. Useful for filtering EDRN biomarkers by tissue or showing tissue names. | Use for: Find EDRN biomarkers associated with a particular anatomical entity; List EDRN biomarkers and their QA state or phase along with tissue names

accepted.name: fda_test_rank_by_gene_count
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  test_trade_name,
  test_submission,
  biomarker_origin,
  doid,
  histological_type,
  specimen_type,
  platform_method,
  test_number_genes,
  test_adoption_evidence,
  test_approval_status,
  test_study_design,
  clinical_significance,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY doid ORDER BY COALESCE(test_number_genes, -1) DESC) AS test_number_genes_rank
FROM biomarker_fda_test
accepted.description: Ranking of biomarker_fda_test rows per doid by test_number_genes in descending order producing a rank column test_number_genes_rank. Useful as a reusable ranking CTE for Top-K tests per disease when combined with a downstream WHERE test_number_genes_rank <= K. | Use for: Select top-K FDA tests by number of genes for a disease (doid); Compare tests within a disease ranked by panel size
